![We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?](assets/40b-cover.png)

# We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their
mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the
[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/by/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163). Let me
tell you a story about it.

**40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a
human.**

That is what building >_Fa — my
[open-source](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness) agent harness
in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in
web [https://fa1.dev](https://fa1.dev).

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds
like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

## The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3,
GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix
looks like this:

| Token type | Volume | ~Rate | ~Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cached reads | ~24B | $0.15 / 1M | ~$3,600 |
| Fresh input | ~14B | $0.60 / 1M | ~$8,400 |
| Output | ~2B | $2.50 / 1M | ~$5,000 |
| **Total** | **40B** | | **≈ $17–20k** |

For scale: the same scope quoted to a dev team — a cross-platform agent
harness, CLI, mobile apps, web app, browser extension, Outlook add-in, CI
automation — is 6–12 months and $300k+. The tokens were ~$20k, and a large
slice of that was burned while I slept.

Still a fuckup-priced hobby? Sure. But here is what actually came out —
feature, and the benefit it buys you.

## The recipe: stand on the shoulders of every harness that annoyed me

I didn't invent >_Fa in a vacuum. I took the best open-source harnesses —
pi, codex, kimi-code, oh-my-pi, later dsh — used them daily, wrote down what
each one did better than the others, and merged those benefits into one Dart
core. The streaming provider contract from pi. The headless discipline of the
CLIs. The "just works in a runner" minimalism.

# Tool availability

**Tool availability** (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model
sees a tool at all: a `tools:` config section stacks four scopes —
global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability
floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate
applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt
no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of
executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform
cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes
(issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is
loaded into the schema at boot (see **Load modes** below).

# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

- The **legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor`** masks values it was told
  about by name (provider API keys, `request_secret` grants). Attached
  lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).
- The **layered `RedactionPipeline`** catches secret-shaped content it was
  never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths
  and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings,
  private-key contexts. Attach point: `attachRedactionPipeline`.

## Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): `registered` (exact values) →

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \

            $targets

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # the build fails without it.
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored too (real keys stay local). The
      # web build needs the file to compile: copy the tracked placeholder —
      # main.dart skips Firebase init for YOUR_* values, so the demo runs
      # without Analytics (as it always has).
      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web demo
        working-directory: flutter_app
        id: web_build
        run: >-
          flutter build web --release
          --base-href /app/
          --output ../build/pages/app

      # The vendored WASI interpreter assets are mobile-only (#1096 AC3):
      # assets/wasm/* loads exclusively through WasiSandboxShell
      # (env_factory_io.dart — Android/iOS); the web build compiles
      # env_factory_stub (wasm_run needs dart:ffi) and runs python/js/
      # sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (web_interpreters_web.dart). ~47MB
      # of dead weight in the deploy root — prune post-build, flags
      # untouched. The extension/office panel builds prune the same set
      # inside their packaging scripts.
      - name: Prune mobile-only wasm interpreter assets (#1096 AC3)
        run: |
          # Shared prune (scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh): fails loudly on
          # flutter_assets layout drift. assets/wasm (~47MB) is loaded
          # exclusively via WasiSandboxShell (mobile-only); the pub
          # package's own test fixtures (coach_anny.glb, 5.6 MB) ride
          # along as package assets nothing on the web app loads.
          bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh build/pages/app/assets \
            assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test

      # The Chrome extension ships on the site too (download + load
      # unpacked): dart2js the SW agent and zip it — flutter is already on
      # PATH here and the script's --with-app embeds the same web build.
      - name: Build Chrome extension
        run: |
          dart pub get
          cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # The Office add-in ships on the site too (sideload from
      # fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml): the script validates the manifest,
      # builds the fa web app with the office host flag (the pane IS the
      # app, outlook/app/) and assembles build/pages/root/outlook/ in
      # place — BEFORE the assemble step, so the artifact dir persists
      # into the upload.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: |
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          cp -R site/. build/pages/root/
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        w…

# Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)

> One agent harness, every device. Fa is an open-source coding agent for Dart and
> Flutter with a real tool loop: a sandboxed shell (curl, wget, jq, yq, rg, sed,
> awk, find, xargs, diff/patch, tar/zip), git over HTTP and SSH, python3 and
> sqlite3 running in the browser, secrets redaction, a file browser, and a
> session tree with context compaction. It runs on iOS, Android, web, desktop,
> as a CLI, as a Chrome extension, and as an Outlook add-in.

## Live demo

- [Try Fa in your browser](https://fa1.dev/app/):
  bring your own key (BYOK). Keys are held in memory only — never persisted —
  and calls go directly from the visitor's browser to the LLM provider.

## Install

- iOS / iPadOS / macOS app — App Store (paid release, funds development):
  https://apps.apple.com/us/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163.
  Free-forever public TestFlight beta:
  https://testflight.apple.com/join/En1eC9UK. Store frames page:
  https://fa1.dev/app-store/. Android: coming soon.
- CLI (macOS, Windows, Linux; requires the Dart SDK, bundled with Flutter):
  `curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/install.sh" | sh`
  or `dart pub global activate flutter_agent_harness`. Both provide the `fah`
  and `fa` executables. Set a provider API key (e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY),
  then run `fah`.
- Flutter demo app from source:
  `git clone https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`, then
  `cd flutter_agent_harness/flutter_app && flutter run`.

## Chrome extension

- MV3 extension that hosts the full Fa web app in a side panel; the agent
  runs in the service worker and drives the browser with 34 tools:
  `tabs_open`, `tabs_close`, `tabs_update`, `tabs_query`, `tabs_move`,
  `tabs_group`, `tabs_ungroup`, `tabs_reload`, `tabs_discard`,
  `windows_open`, `windows_update`, `windows_close`, `windows_list`,
  `groups_update`, `groups_close`, `sessions_recent`, `sessions_restore`,
  `history_search`, `bookmarks_list`, `bookmarks_add`, `bookmarks_update`,
  `bookmarks_remove`, `downloads_start`, `downloads_search`,
  `downloads_cancel`, `cookies_get`, `cookies_set`, `cookies_remove`,
  `inject_js`, `inject_css`, `cdp_eval`, `page_screenshot`,
  `app_screenshot`, `nav_wait` — plus four Settings-gated second-tier
  tools that surface once the user enables them:
  `browser_search`, `top_sites`, `reading_list`, `page_capture`.
- Entry points: the side panel, the omnibox (`fa <query>`), the
  Ctrl+Shift+1 hotkey, and the context menu on any selection. Page-derived
  content is quarantined as untrusted data. `inject_js` prompts on every
  call in every session mode by default — explicitly switching the
  session to yolo drops that guard (the override is cleared, not
  bypassed silently).
- Artifact (rebuilt on every deploy):
  https://fa1.dev/extension/fa-extension.zip — unzip, then open
  chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, Load unpacked, pick the
  unzipped folder.
- Architecture and operations: `docs/browser-extension.md` in the repository.

## Outlook add-in

- Fa as an Office Add-in taskpane (MailApp manifest with a
  VersionOverrides command surface, Mailbox 1.8+, ReadWriteItem
  permission): the same pure-Dart agent core plus three mail
  tools — `outlook.read_current_item` (metadata + body of the open email),
  `outlook.read_attachment` (one attachment, base64, 50 MB cap), and
  `outlook.insert_draft_body` (compose mode). Attachment reads and draft
  writes always prompt for approval.
- Email bodies and attachments enter the model context only inside a
  quarantine fence marked as untrusted data, so instructions inside a
  message can never drive the agent.
- Manifest artifact: https://fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml — download it,
  open https://aka.ms/olksideload (My add-ins), then Custom add-ins →
  "+ Add a custom add-in" → Add from file → manifest.xml → Install.
  Microsoft removed the manual "Add from a URL" entry, so
  download-then-file is the only self-service install path (works in
  Outlook on the web, new Outlook for Windows, and classic Outlook;
  tenants that block custom add-ins need an admin deployment or a
  personal Outlook.com account). Entry point per client (manifest ≥
  1.1.0.0): new Outlook for Windows and OWA show the «fa» button in a
  message's Apps flyout, classic Outlook on the Home ribbon. The
  taskpane page lives at https://fa1.dev/outlook/; full step-by-step
  guide with troubleshooting: https://fa1.dev/outlook/support.html
- Sources: `office_addin/` in the repository.

## Agent tools (every platform)

- Core tools on every host: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `ls`, `bash`
  (plus background `bash_job`), `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `task`
  (parallel subagents: explore/review/plan; managed with `task_status`,
  `task_send`, `task_observe`, `task_cancel`), `lsp`,
  `memory_add`, `memory_delete`, `memory_list`, `memory_search`,
  `checkpoint`, `rewind`, `ask`, `request_secret`, `config`,
  `agent_message`, `agent_directory`, `schedule_message`, `reply`,
  `transcribe_audio`, `inspect_image`, `generate_image`, `generate_video`.
- MCP: any server configured in `~/.fah/config.yaml` registers its tools
  as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.
- CLI browser bridge: `fa serve --bridge` + `/browser connect` pairs a
  desktop agent with the extension for `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`,
  `browser_type`, `browser_press_key`, `browser_select`, `browser_tabs`,
  `browser_switch_tab`, `browser_read_dom`, `browser_screenshot`,
  `browser_eval`, `browser_wait_for`.
- The shell behind `bash`: pure-Dart builtins on web, WASI binaries
  (uutils coreutils, ripgrep, python3, sqlite3) on iOS/Android, the host
  shell on macOS/Windows/Linux.

## Project

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness)
- [pub.dev package](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_agent_harness)
- [Issue tracker](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues)

## Key facts

- Written in Dart; the core library is pure Dart (no dart:io) and compiles to web.
- Providers: OpenAI-compatible (incl. OpenRouter and Ollama Cloud), Anthropic, Google.
- Web sandbox is a pure-Dart in-memory shell; mobile uses WASI binaries
  (uutils coreutils, ripgrep, sed/awk, python3, sqlite3, lua) under an embedded
  wasm runtime.
- Ships as: CLI (`fa`/`fah`), Flutter apps (iOS/Android/macOS/Windows/Linux),
  a static web app, a Chrome MV3 extension, and an Outlook Office add-in.
- License: MIT. Published on pub.dev as `flutter_agent_harness`.

## FAQ (quotable answers)

- What is Fa? An open-source coding agent for Dart and Flutter: a pure-Dart
  agent core plus a sandboxed workbench (shell, git, python3, sqlite3) running
  identically on iOS, Android, web, desktop, and as a CLI — plus a Chrome
  extension and an Outlook add-in on the same core.
- Is the API key safe in the web demo? Yes: memory-only (never persisted to
  localStorage/cookies/disk, gone on reload), and calls go directly from the
  browser to the provider — the page is static files, no server or proxy.
- Which providers? OpenAI-compatible endpoints (OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud,
  self-hosted llama.cpp/LM Studio/vLLM), Anthropic, Google; custom endpoints
  with a base URL, with model list/context window/output caps auto-detected.
- Which platforms? iOS, Android, web (static files), macOS, Windows, Linux,
  CLI — plus a Chrome MV3 extension and an Outlook Office add-in.
- What can the agent do? Shell (curl, jq, rg, sed/awk, tar/zip, diff/patch),
  git clone/push over HTTP and SSH, python3 with pip, sqlite3, QuickJS, file
  edits, web search/fetch, subagents, LSP, MCP tools, persistent memory,
  checkpoint/rewind, and long sessions with automatic context compaction;
  the Chrome extension adds 34 browser tools, Outlook adds three mail tools.
- Is it free? The project is MIT-licensed open source; users pay their own LLM
  provider for tokens only — no subscription or account.
- How to install the CLI? `curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/install.sh" | sh`
  (or `dart pub global activate flutter_agent_harness`), then run `fa`.
- How do I install the Chrome extension? Download
  https://fa1.dev/extension/fa-extension.zip, unzip it, then
  chrome://extensions → Developer mode → Load unpacked.

# We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their
mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the
[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/by/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163). Let me
tell you a story about it.

**40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a
human.**

That is what building >_Fa — my
[open-source](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness) agent harness
in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in
web [https://fa1.dev](https://fa1.dev).

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds
like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

## The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3,
GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix
looks like this:

| Token type | Volume | ~Rate | ~Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cached reads | ~24B | $0.15 / 1M | ~$3,600 |
| Fresh input | ~14B | $0.60 / 1M | ~$8,400 |
| Output | ~2B | $2.50 / 1M | ~$5,000 |
| **Total** | **40B** | | **≈ $17–20k** |

For scale: the same scope quoted to a dev team — a cross-platform agent
harness, CLI, mobile apps, web app, browser extension, Outlook add-in, CI
automation — is 6–12 months and $300k+. The tokens were ~$20k, and a large
slice of that was burned while I slept.

Still a fuckup-priced hobby? Sure. But here is what actually came out —
feature, and the benefit it buys you.

## The recipe: stand on the shoulders of every harness that annoyed me

I didn't invent >_Fa in a vacuum. I took the best open-source harnesses —
pi, codex, kimi-code, oh-my-pi, later dsh — used them daily, wrote down what
each one did better than the others, and merged those benefits into one Dart
core. The streaming provider contract from pi. The headless discipline of the
CLIs. The "just works in a runner" minimalism.

# Tool availability

**Tool availability** (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model
sees a tool at all: a `tools:` config section stacks four scopes —
global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability
floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate
applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt
no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of
executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform
cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes
(issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is
loaded into the schema at boot (see **Load modes** below).

# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

      - name: Format coverage to lcov

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
.git/hooks/pre-merge-commit.sample:11:test -x "$GIT_DIR/hooks/pre-commit" &&
.git/hooks/pre-merge-commit.sample:12:        exec "$GIT_DIR/hooks/pre-commit"
.git/hooks/pre-applypatch.sample:12:precommit="$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-commit)"

blocks.text:
# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.

- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…
