#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

I'll write a throwaway script in /tmp and run it. Indentation: JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ') produces 2-space indent matching existing style. Key order: Dart maps preserve insertion order; JSON parse preserves order too (json.decode returns LinkedHashMap with source order).

# Fa (Flutter Agent Harness)

> One agent harness, every device. Fa is an open-source coding agent for Dart and
> Flutter with a real tool loop: a sandboxed shell (curl, wget, jq, yq, rg, sed,
> awk, find, xargs, diff/patch, tar/zip), git over HTTP and SSH, python3 and
> sqlite3 running in the browser, secrets redaction, a file browser, and a
> session tree with context compaction. It runs on iOS, Android, web, desktop,
> as a CLI, as a Chrome extension, and as an Outlook add-in.

## Live demo

- [Try Fa in your browser](https://fa1.dev/app/):
  bring your own key (BYOK). Keys are held in memory only — never persisted —
  and calls go directly from the visitor's browser to the LLM provider.

## Install

- iOS / iPadOS / macOS app — App Store (paid release, funds development):
  https://apps.apple.com/us/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163.
  Free-forever public TestFlight beta:
  https://testflight.apple.com/join/En1eC9UK. Store frames page:
  https://fa1.dev/app-store/. Android: coming soon.
- CLI (macOS, Windows, Linux; requires the Dart SDK, bundled with Flutter):

  `windows_open`, `windows_update`, `windows_close`, `windows_list`,

  `app_screenshot`, `nav_wait` — plus four Settings-gated second-tier
  tools that surface once the user enables them:

# We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their
mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the
[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/by/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163). Let me
tell you a story about it.

**40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a
human.**

That is what building >_Fa — my
[open-source](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness) agent harness
in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in
web [https://fa1.dev](https://fa1.dev).

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds
like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

## The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3,
GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix
looks like this:

| Token type | Volume | ~Rate | ~Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cached reads | ~24B | $0.15 / 1M | ~$3,600 |
| Fresh input | ~14B | $0.60 / 1M | ~$8,400 |
| Output | ~2B | $2.50 / 1M | ~$5,000 |
| **Total** | **40B** | | **≈ $17–20k** |

For scale: the same scope quoted to a dev team — a cross-platform agent
harness, CLI, mobile apps, web app, browser extension, Outlook add-in, CI
automation — is 6–12 months and $300k+. The tokens were ~$20k, and a large
slice of that was burned while I slept.

Still a fuckup-priced hobby? Sure. But here is what actually came out —
feature, and the benefit it buys you.

## The recipe: stand on the shoulders of every harness that annoyed me

I didn't invent >_Fa in a vacuum. I took the best open-source harnesses —
pi, codex, kimi-code, oh-my-pi, later dsh — used them daily, wrote down what
each one did better than the others, and merged those benefits into one Dart
core. The streaming provider contract from pi. The headless discipline of the
CLIs. The "just works in a runner" minimalism.

# Tool availability

**Tool availability** (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model
sees a tool at all: a `tools:` config section stacks four scopes —
global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability
floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate
applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt
no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of
executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform
cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes
(issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is
loaded into the schema at boot (see **Load modes** below).

# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

- The **legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor`** masks values it was told
  about by name (provider API keys, `request_secret` grants). Attached
  lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).
- The **layered `RedactionPipeline`** catches secret-shaped content it was
  never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths
  and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings,
  private-key contexts. Attach point: `attachRedactionPipeline`.

## Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): `registered` (exact values) →

My script rendering from site/blog/posts/*.md builds on the committed copies. That's simplest and self-contained — the site tree is the deploy unit. However lastmod from git: use file mtime or git log. In CI, git log works; on local runners too (shallow clones? git log of a file works in shallow clone as long as the file's history... shallow clone might not have history of the file — use `git log -1 --format=%cs -- <path>` and fall back to mtime/ front-matter date.

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.

if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then

  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

![We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?](assets/40b-cover.png)

# We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their
mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the
[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/by/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163). Let me
tell you a story about it.

**40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a
human.**

That is what building >_Fa — my
[open-source](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness) agent harness
in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in
web [https://fa1.dev](https://fa1.dev).

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds
like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

## The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3,
GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix
looks like this:

| Token type | Volume | ~Rate | ~Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cached reads | ~24B | $0.15 / 1M | ~$3,600 |
| Fresh input | ~14B | $0.60 / 1M | ~$8,400 |
| Output | ~2B | $2.50 / 1M | ~$5,000 |
| **Total** | **40B** | | **≈ $17–20k** |

For scale: the same scope quoted to a dev team — a cross-platform agent
harness, CLI, mobile apps, web app, browser extension, Outlook add-in, CI
automation — is 6–12 months and $300k+. The tokens were ~$20k, and a large
slice of that was burned while I slept.

Still a fuckup-priced hobby? Sure. But here is what actually came out —
feature, and the benefit it buys you.

## The recipe: stand on the shoulders of every harness that annoyed me

I didn't invent >_Fa in a vacuum. I took the best open-source harnesses —
pi, codex, kimi-code, oh-my-pi, later dsh — used them daily, wrote down what
each one did better than the others, and merged those benefits into one Dart
core. The streaming provider contract from pi. The headless discipline of the
CLIs. The "just works in a runner" minimalism.

# Tool availability

**Tool availability** (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model
sees a tool at all: a `tools:` config section stacks four scopes —
global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability
floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate
applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt
no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of
executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform
cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes
(issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is
loaded into the schema at boot (see **Load modes** below).

# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

- The **legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor`** masks values it was told
  about by name (provider API keys, `request_secret` grants). Attached
  lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).
- The **layered `RedactionPipeline`** catches secret-shaped content it was
  never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths
  and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings,
  private-key contexts. Attach point: `attachRedactionPipeline`.

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

# Tool availability

**Tool availability** (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model
sees a tool at all: a `tools:` config section stacks four scopes —
global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability
floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate
applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt
no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of
executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform
cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes
(issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is
loaded into the schema at boot (see **Load modes** below).

## A full example

```yaml
# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:

# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

- The **legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor`** masks values it was told
  about by name (provider API keys, `request_secret` grants). Attached
  lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).
- The **layered `RedactionPipeline`** catches secret-shaped content it was
  never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }

            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the

# Tool availability

**Tool availability** (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model
sees a tool at all: a `tools:` config section stacks four scopes —
global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability
floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate
applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt
no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of
executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform
cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes
(issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is
loaded into the schema at boot (see **Load modes** below).

# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

- The **legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor`** masks values it was told
  about by name (provider API keys, `request_secret` grants). Attached
  lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).
- The **layered `RedactionPipeline`** catches secret-shaped content it was
  never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths
  and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings,
  private-key contexts. Attach point: `attachRedactionPipeline`.

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║

# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

# Tool availability

**Tool availability** (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model
sees a tool at all: a `tools:` config section stacks four scopes —
global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability
floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate
applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt
no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of
executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform
cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes
(issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is
loaded into the schema at boot (see **Load modes** below).

# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

- The **legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor`** masks values it was told
  about by name (provider API keys, `request_secret` grants). Attached
  lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).
- The **layered `RedactionPipeline`** catches secret-shaped content it was
  never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths
  and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings,
  private-key contexts. Attach point: `attachRedactionPipeline`.

## Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): `registered` (exact values) →

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

Rather than retyping the entire FAQPage and HowTo content (huge, error-prone), I'll do this surgically with a small script: parse index.html, extract the three JSON blocks, wrap nodes into @graph. Actually simpler: do the edit with a python/dart one-liner that:
1. Reads site/index.html.
2. Extracts the three `<script type="application/ld+json">...</script>` blocks, parses JSON, takes each object's content minus @context.
3. Builds new structure: @context + @graph [Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication (modified author → @id, + sameAs), SoftwareSourceCode, FAQPage, HowTo].
4. Writes back.

JSON pretty-print formatting will change (indent 2, same style). That's acceptable — "intentionally extended". But byte-stability REG for the *content*: text strings unchanged.

I'll write a throwaway script in /tmp and run it. Indentation: JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ') produces 2-space indent matching existing style. Key order: Dart maps preserve insertion order; JSON parse preserves order too (json.decode returns LinkedHashMap with source order).

# Tool availability

**Tool availability** (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model
sees a tool at all: a `tools:` config section stacks four scopes —
global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability
floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate
applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt
no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of
executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform
cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes
(issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is
loaded into the schema at boot (see **Load modes** below).

## A full example

```yaml

# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

- The **legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor`** masks values it was told
  about by name (provider API keys, `request_secret` grants). Attached
  lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).
- The **layered `RedactionPipeline`** catches secret-shaped content it was
  never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths
  and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings,
  private-key contexts. Attach point: `attachRedactionPipeline`.

## Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): `registered` (exact values) →

The ticket is huge. I'll implement D1–D5 fully with a Dart build script + tests + CI wiring. Given the repo conventions (TDD, tests in `test/`), and existing guards in `test/site/`, I'll write:

### 1. `scripts/build_site.dart` — the static pre-render build (D1, D4, llms-full)

Pure Dart + dart:io, no deps. Responsibilities:
- **Blog pre-render**: read `site/blog/posts/*.md` (the committed copies — actually canonical source is `blog/posts/`; build_blog.dart copies. Hmm. Which to render from? To keep one source of truth I'll render from `site/blog/posts/*.md` — the copies that are already in the site tree and committed. But wait: build_blog.dart copies from blog/posts to site/blog/posts, and the md copies are committed. If someone edits blog/posts/*.md they must run build_blog.dart. My script rendering from site/blog/posts/*.md builds on the committed copies. That's simplest and self-contained — the site tree is the deploy unit. However lastmod from git: use file mtime or git log. In CI, git log works; on local runners too (shallow clones? git log of a file works in shallow clone as long as the file's history... shallow clone might not have history of the file — use `git log -1 --format=%cs -- <path>` and fall back to mtime/ front-matter date.

Actually for determinism across environments, better: lastmod = max(git last-commit date for the source md, front-matter date). Determinism matters for the "CI fails on stale generated artifacts" check — the check rebuilds and diffs; if the builder is deterministic given the sources, diffs only appear when sources change. Using git log in the builder is fine since CI runs the same command. But mtime is NOT deterministic (checkout sets mtime to checkout time). So prefer git log, fall back to front-matter date.

Hmm, but wait — determinism across `git clone` depth: Actions checkout default fetch-depth=1 — file history unavailable! `git log -1 -- path` on a shallow clone returns nothing for old files. Then fall back: front-matter `date` for posts; for sitemap pages... we need per-page lastmod. Options: maintain a small static registry in the build script of page → source file mapping, using git log with fallbacks. This could get fragile.

Alternative simpler robust approach: **mtime-based** with explicit pinning. The sitemap's lastmod for hand-maintained pages (index.html etc.) — I could compute from git when available, else mtime. The CI staleness check would run the builder and diff; both in CI run on a fresh checkout with same mtimes? No — the CI check runs `dart run scripts/build_site.dart --check` (or rebuild + git diff --exit-code). If lastmod depends on mtime, checkout in CI has fresh mtimes for ALL files (roughly the same second), so diff would be stable within one run (both committed file and regenerated file derive lastmod from the same checkout mtimes). Wait, the check: rebuild writes sitemap.xml; then `git diff --exit-code site/sitemap.xml`. If builder uses mtime, regenerated lastmod == checkout mtime of sources; committed sitemap has older dates → diff fails always. Bad.

So determinism demands git-history or pinned values. In a fetch-depth=1 checkout, git log gives commit date for all files at HEAD (the single commit). That would make every page's lastmod = HEAD commit date → changes on every commit → committed sitemap always stale. Also bad.

Practical approach used by many: keep an explicit `lastmod` registry for static pages in the build script (hand-maintained, like current sitemap), and derive blog post lastmod from front-matter `date` + git log override when deeper history is available. Hmm, but ticket says "real lastmod (file mtime / git log)" and "hand-maintained (drifts)" is the complaint for G5.

Let me reconsider: what does the CI staleness check need? It needs: sources (md files, docs list, page registry) → generated artifacts. Deterministic. So the builder must be a pure function of committed inputs. Git history is NOT available reliably in shallow CI checkouts. File mtimes are not committed. Therefore **the only committed time signal is content itself** (front-matter dates) plus an explicit registry in the script.

Design: build script contains:
- `_staticPages`: list of (url path, source file, changefreq, priority) — lastmod derived from front-matter/mapping or a per-page `lastmod:` field in the registry that humans bump when they edit the page (same as today but centralized and CI-checked against... hmm, that drifts again — that's the current problem).

Alternative: use `git log -1 --format=%cs --follow -- <file>` and if empty (shallow), fall back to a committed `lastmod` in registry. In full clones (local dev, pre-commit hook maybe), git gives true dates. In CI shallow checkouts, fallback to registry values — which are committed, so deterministic. When a page is edited in a PR, CI's shallow checkout: file changed in the PR's HEAD commit → git log finds HEAD date → regenerated sitemap has today's date ≠ committed (author didn't rebuild or committed regenerated... author commits regenerated sitemap from local full clone where git log gives real last commit date of that file — which for a file changed in the PR equals the PR branch's last commit touching it, whose date differs from what CI computes at HEAD? No wait: CI checkout of the PR merge commit — the file's last commit in the shallow history is the merge/squash commit... ugh, after squash-merge, all files' last commit = the squash commit = merge date, while author regenerated pre-merge with the branch's commit date. → diff. This is getting too clever. 

Simplest bulletproof: **lastmod = front-matter `date` for posts; registry `lastmod` in build script for static pages, enforced by a drift check** — the drift check: for each static page, registry lastmod must be ≥ mtime-derived... no.

OK step back. What really matters per acceptance: "Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema" and "CI fails on stale generated artifacts". A pragmatic, defensible implementation:

- Posts: lastmod from front-matter `date` (real, committed, single-source). For dateModified, same. Good enough and deterministic.
- Static pages: keep explicit `lastmod` values in the build script registry (like today) — but add a CI **drift guard test**: for each registered page, `git log -1 --format=%cs -- <page>` (when history available, e.g. nightly/full clones) must be ≤ registry lastmod... that fails the other direction.

Honestly, the industry-standard answer: derive lastmod from git log, run CI checkouts with fetch-depth: 0, and have the CI check rebuild+diff. Locally, devs run the same builder. Squash-merge: after merge, the committed sitemap (built on the branch) may have lastmod dates from branch commits; CI on main rebuilds → dates become merge commit dates for changed files → diff → red on main. That WOULD break. Unless post-merge regeneration is automated (daily job commits regen). Too much machinery for this card.

Pragmatic compromise (and I'll document it in the script): 
- lastmod for generated pages (blog posts, docs) = front-matter date / explicit per-doc date (committed, deterministic).

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║

# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

Works, but inner nodes kept their `"@context": "https://schema.org"` keys — redundant inside a @graph (harmless but sloppy; schema.org validators tolerate it, but cleaner to strip). Also array formatting: JsonEncoder.withIndent puts each element on its own line — acceptable but verbose for sameAs arrays of 1-2 items. Fine.

Let me strip the nested @context keys from graph nodes (except top). Quick tweak: in the transform, remove '@context' from each node. Also compact arrays? Leave. Re-run: but the transform already consumed the 3-block format. Easier: small sed-like edit via dart one-liner to remove the two `"@context": "https://schema.org",` lines that are inside graph nodes (lines 71-ish and the FAQPage one). They appear at known indentation (4 spaces). Lines: `    {` followed by `      "@context": "https://schema.org",`. Use python or dart to remove lines matching `^      "@context": "https://schema.org",$` — the top-level one has 2-space indent `  "@context"`. Let me do it.

## Scope decisions

The ticket is huge. I'll implement D1–D5 fully with a Dart build script + tests + CI wiring. Given the repo conventions (TDD, tests in `test/`), and existing guards in `test/site/`, I'll write:

### 1. `scripts/build_site.dart` — the static pre-render build (D1, D4, llms-full)

Pure Dart + dart:io, no deps. Responsibilities:
- **Blog pre-render**: read `site/blog/posts/*.md` (the committed copies — actually canonical source is `blog/posts/`; build_blog.dart copies. Hmm. Which to render from? To keep one source of truth I'll render from `site/blog/posts/*.md` — the copies that are already in the site tree and committed. But wait: build_blog.dart copies from blog/posts to site/blog/posts, and the md copies are committed. If someone edits blog/posts/*.md they must run build_blog.dart. My script rendering from site/blog/posts/*.md builds on the committed copies. That's simplest and self-contained — the site tree is the deploy unit. However lastmod from git: use file mtime or git log. In CI, git log works; on local runners too (shallow clones? git log of a file works in shallow clone as long as the file's history... shallow clone might not have history of the file — use `git log -1 --format=%cs -- <path>` and fall back to mtime/ front-matter date.

Actually for determinism across environments, better: lastmod = max(git last-commit date for the source md, front-matter date). Determinism matters for the "CI fails on stale generated artifacts" check — the check rebuilds and diffs; if the builder is deterministic given the sources, diffs only appear when sources change. Using git log in the builder is fine since CI runs the same command. But mtime is NOT deterministic (checkout sets mtime to checkout time). So prefer git log, fall back to front-matter date.

Hmm, but wait — determinism across `git clone` depth: Actions checkout default fetch-depth=1 — file history unavailable! `git log -1 -- path` on a shallow clone returns nothing for old files. Then fall back: front-matter `date` for posts; for sitemap pages... we need per-page lastmod. Options: maintain a small static registry in the build script of page → source file mapping, using git log with fallbacks. This could get fragile.

Alternative simpler robust approach: **mtime-based** with explicit pinning. The sitemap's lastmod for hand-maintained pages (index.html etc.) — I could compute from git when available, else mtime. The CI staleness check would run the builder and diff; both in CI run on a fresh checkout with same mtimes? No — the CI check runs `dart run scripts/build_site.dart --check` (or rebuild + git diff --exit-code). If lastmod depends on mtime, checkout in CI has fresh mtimes for ALL files (roughly the same second), so diff would be stable within one run (both committed file and regenerated file derive lastmod from the same checkout mtimes). Wait, the check: rebuild writes sitemap.xml; then `git diff --exit-code site/sitemap.xml`. If builder uses mtime, regenerated lastmod == checkout mtime of sources; committed sitemap has older dates → diff fails always. Bad.

So determinism demands git-history or pinned values. In a fetch-depth=1 checkout, git log gives commit date for all files at HEAD (the single commit). That would make every page's lastmod = HEAD commit date → changes on every commit → committed sitemap always stale. Also bad.

Practical approach used by many: keep an explicit `lastmod` registry for static pages in the build script (hand-maintained, like current sitemap), and derive blog post lastmod from front-matter `date` + git log override when deeper history is available. Hmm, but ticket says "real lastmod (file mtime / git log)" and "hand-maintained (drifts)" is the complaint for G5.

Let me reconsider: what does the CI staleness check need? It needs: sources (md files, docs list, page registry) → generated artifacts. Deterministic. So the builder must be a pure function of committed inputs. Git history is NOT available reliably in shallow CI checkouts. File mtimes are not committed. Therefore **the only committed time signal is content itself** (front-matter dates) plus an explicit registry in the script.

Design: build script contains:
- `_staticPages`: list of (url path, source file, changefreq, priority) — lastmod derived from front-matter/mapping or a per-page `lastmod:` field in the registry that humans bump when they edit the page (same as today but centralized and CI-checked against... hmm, that drifts again — that's the current problem).

Alternative: use `git log -1 --format=%cs --follow -- <file>` and if empty (shallow), fall back to a committed `lastmod` in registry. In full clones (local dev, pre-commit hook maybe), git gives true dates. In CI shallow checkouts, fallback to registry values — which are committed, so deterministic. When a page is edited in a PR, CI's shallow checkout: file changed in the PR's HEAD commit → git log finds HEAD date → regenerated sitemap has today's date ≠ committed (author didn't rebuild or committed regenerated... author commits regenerated sitemap from local full clone where git log gives real last commit date of that file — which for a file changed in the PR equals the PR branch's last commit touching it, whose date differs from what CI computes at HEAD? No wait: CI checkout of the PR merge commit — the file's last commit in the shallow history is the merge/squash commit... ugh, after squash-merge, all files' last commit = the squash commit = merge date, while author regenerated pre-merge with the branch's commit date. → diff. This is getting too clever. 

Simplest bulletproof: **lastmod = front-matter `date` for posts; registry `lastmod` in build script for static pages, enforced by a drift check** — the drift check: for each static page, registry lastmod must be ≥ mtime-derived... no.

OK step back. What really matters per acceptance: "Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema" and "CI fails on stale generated artifacts". A pragmatic, defensible implementation:

- Posts: lastmod from front-matter `date` (real, committed, single-source). For dateModified, same. Good enough and deterministic.
- Static pages: keep explicit `lastmod` values in the build script registry (like today) — but add a CI **drift guard test**: for each registered page, `git log -1 --format=%cs -- <page>` (when history available, e.g. nightly/full clones) must be ≤ registry lastmod... that fails the other direction.

Honestly, the industry-standard answer: derive lastmod from git log, run CI checkouts with fetch-depth: 0, and have the CI check rebuild+diff. Locally, devs run the same builder. Squash-merge: after merge, the committed sitemap (built on the branch) may have lastmod dates from branch commits; CI on main rebuilds → dates become merge commit dates for changed files → diff → red on main. That WOULD break. Unless post-merge regeneration is automated (daily job commits regen). Too much machinery for this card.

Pragmatic compromise (and I'll document it in the script): 
- lastmod for generated pages (blog posts, docs) = front-matter date / explicit per-doc date (committed, deterministic).
- lastmod for static pages = registry in the build script, bumped via a test that warns... 

Actually wait — simpler: for static pages use the mtime of the source file AT BUILD TIME, but store it... no.

Decision: I'll use git log when available with graceful fallback, AND make the CI staleness check operate in a mode tolerant of that: the CI check (`--check`) compares generated output against committed files **excluding lastmod lines?** No — weak.

Cleaner: The CI check test will be a *deterministic-content* check: rebuild into a temp dir and diff ignoring `<lastmod>` lines? Hmm, but then stale lastmod never caught...

static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

>_ Fa fa1.dev

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

messages.preview: No markdown package — I'll hand-roll a minimal renderer per repo convention ("Pure Dart + dart:io, no package deps"). Let me look at the `static:` CI job and the rest of the post markdown to know what…

blocks.text:
No markdown package in deps. I could add `markdown: ^7.0.0` as a dev_dependency — that's cleaner and battle-tested for GFM tables etc. Adding a dev dep requires lockfile update (`dart pub get`), and lockfile check CI (check_lockfiles.sh). Adding a dev_dependency is acceptable and much safer than hand-rolling markdown. But wait — scripts run in CI with `dart pub get`? The ci jobs run dart pub get anyway. `package:markdown` supports GFM via `markdownToHtml(body, extensionSet: ExtensionSet.gitHubWeb)`... Actually GitHubWeb includes tables, fenced code, strikethrough, auto-links. 

Hmm, but does adding a dependency risk the vendor/lockfile gates? check_lockfiles_gate_test.dart — checks lockfiles are in sync; running `dart pub get` regenerates pubspec.lock which I commit. Should be fine.

Alternatively hand-roll. package:markdown is pure Dart, well-tested, zero risk to runtime (dev_dependency + script uses it... scripts are run with `dart run` from root package, so dependency must be a regular dependency, not dev — scripts/ is part of the root package. dev_dependencies are available to `dart run` too? dev_dependencies ARE resolved for the root package, and scripts/ code is part of root package, so yes, dev_dependency works for scripts and tests. `dart run scripts/build_blog.dart` works today with only dev deps... build_blog uses no packages. gen_prompts? uses yaml probably (dev dep). So put `markdown` in dev_dependencies.

Let me confirm network availability for pub get — CI runner, may have network. Let me try `dart pub get` later and see if it can fetch. If no network, hand-roll the renderer. Let me check quickly whether there's a pub cache with markdown already (vendor/?). Check `ls vendor/` and `dart pub cache`? Try adding and running pub get; if offline, revert to hand-rolled.

Actually — decision: hand-roll a minimal renderer. Reasons: (1) no network risk, (2) no lockfile churn, (3) full control over output determinism, (4) repo convention explicitly states "Pure Dart + dart:io, no package deps" for scripts. The blog posts are the only markdown being rendered, and I can look at what constructs they use. Tables, headings, bold, links, images, lists, hr, blockquote maybe. A ~200-line renderer with tests. Determinism is fully in hand.

Now the plan:

**Files to create/modify:**
1. `scripts/build_site.dart` (new) — builder library + main.
2. `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart` (new) — TDD unit tests for renderer, frontmatter, sitemap gen, llms-full assembly, BlogPosting/TechArticle JSON.
3. `test/site_geo_test.dart` (new) — no-JS crawl test (HTTP serve), sitemap integrity, schema validation, robots contract, llms-full budget.
4. `site/robots.txt` (rewrite — D2).
5. `site/index.html` (JSON-LD @graph merge — D3).
6. `site/llms.txt` (extend: blog + docs + llms-full pointer).
