blocks.text:
Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

`: the body md already starts with `# ` (the post md has its own H1), and my template adds `<h1>$title</h1>`. Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Fix: alignFor returns String? — change signature: `String? alignFor(int col) => col < aligns.length ? aligns[col] : null;` 3. `'` escaping of apostrophes in text — fine (valid HTML). 4. Two-space/indent quirk: `$meta$bodyHtml </article>` — bodyHtml lines start at col 0; fine. 5. Duplicate h1 also in docs pages? DocsPage body drops the first H1 — good. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Fix the builder: - In renderBlogPostPage: preprocess body: split lines; drop leading blank lines; if first line is `# <title-ish>` → drop; if first non-empty line is `![...](<cover>)` → drop and forceCover=true. Then html = renderMarkdown. Cover img emitted when `cover != null && (forcedCover || !body.includes...)` — after stripping, always emit post-cover when cover != null and we stripped it; if not stripped (cover not in body), emit post-cover too (post.html behavior). So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. Also meta date: fine. Fix alignFor now. Also check: in `_renderTable`, `alignFor` used `aligns[col] != null ? aligns[col]! : ''` — replace with nullable.
Two bugs to fix: duplicate `<h1>`/cover (post body has its own) and empty `text-align` in tables.

The H1 strip didn't work — still a duplicate `<h1>` in body. Why? plainText comparison: title = "We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?`. plainText strips `[`*_~#>]` — the `~` in `(~$20k)` gets stripped! plainText removes `~` chars → "($20k)" vs title plainText also strips → both stripped equally. Wait both sides go through plainText... title has `(~$20k)` → plainText → `($20k)`; h1 same → equal. Hmm should match.

Wait — maybe the first line isn't the h1. Body after stripFrontmatter: the md begins with a blank line, then `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)`, then blank, then `# title`. So order: image FIRST, then h1! My code checks h1 first, then image. The first non-empty line is the image; h1 check fails on the image line; then cover-image check: start points at image line → matches → start++ → then the `# title` line remains in body.

Fix: handle sequence: loop — skip blanks; if line is cover image (and cover != null and not yet stripped) → strip; else if h1 == title → strip; else stop. Both, in either order.

Updated 2026-10-10 · IstiN

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: false                  # per-server granularity (mcp:<server>)

# <project>/.fah/config.yaml — PROJECT scope: travels with the repo.
tools:
====
href="../../"
href="../../#demo"
href="../../#features"
href="../../#install"
href="../../blog/"
href="../../favicon.svg?v=2"
href="../../styles.css?v=3"
href="../../widgets/"
href="https://fa1.dev/docs/tool-availability/"
href="https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness"

  • The legacy exact-value SecretRedactor masks values it was told

about by name (provider API keys, request_secret grants). Attached lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).

  • The layered RedactionPipeline catches secret-shaped content it was

never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings, private-key contexts. Attach point: attachRedactionPipeline.

Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): registered (exact values) → path (credential files) → credential (DOM form-field values) → vendor (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → prefix (indexOf pre-screen feeding vendor) → pem → asn1 → connection → context (password/secret key names) → entropy → pii (off by default). Output markers are [REDACTED:<kind>], idempotent, and line-count preserving. Allowlisted shapes (Git SHAs, UUIDs) and data: base64 URLs survive.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

blocks.text:
Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

`: the body md already starts with `# ` (the post md has its own H1), and my template adds `<h1>$title</h1>`. Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Fix: alignFor returns String? — change signature: `String? alignFor(int col) => col < aligns.length ? aligns[col] : null;` 3. `'` escaping of apostrophes in text — fine (valid HTML). 4. Two-space/indent quirk: `$meta$bodyHtml </article>` — bodyHtml lines start at col 0; fine. 5. Duplicate h1 also in docs pages? DocsPage body drops the first H1 — good. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Fix the builder: - In renderBlogPostPage: preprocess body: split lines; drop leading blank lines; if first line is `# <title-ish>` → drop; if first non-empty line is `![...](<cover>)` → drop and forceCover=true. Then html = renderMarkdown. Cover img emitted when `cover != null && (forcedCover || !body.includes...)` — after stripping, always emit post-cover when cover != null and we stripped it; if not stripped (cover not in body), emit post-cover too (post.html behavior). So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. Also meta date: fine. Fix alignFor now. Also check: in `_renderTable`, `alignFor` used `aligns[col] != null ? aligns[col]! : ''` — replace with nullable.
Two bugs to fix: duplicate `<h1>`/cover (post body has its own) and empty `text-align` in tables.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision.   • The legacy exact-value SecretRedactor masks values it was told

about by name (provider API keys, request_secret grants). Attached lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).

  • The layered RedactionPipeline catches secret-shaped content it was

never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings, private-key contexts. Attach point: attachRedactionPipeline.

Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): registered (exact values) → path (credential files) → credential (DOM form-field values) → vendor (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → prefix (indexOf pre-screen feeding vendor) → pem → asn1 → connection → context (password/secret key names) → entropy → pii (off by default). Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Then html = renderMarkdown. So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. Also meta date: fine. Fix alignFor now. Also check: in `_renderTable`, `alignFor` used `aligns[col] != null ? aligns[col]! : ''` — replace with nullable.

Updated 2026-10-10 · IstiN

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: false                  # per-server granularity (mcp:<server>)

# <project>/.fah/config.yaml — PROJECT scope: travels with the repo.
tools:

  • The legacy exact-value SecretRedactor masks values it was told

about by name (provider API keys, request_secret grants). Attached lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).

  • The layered RedactionPipeline catches secret-shaped content it was

never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings, private-key contexts. Attach point: attachRedactionPipeline.

Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): registered (exact values) → path (credential files) → credential (DOM form-field values) → vendor (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → prefix (indexOf pre-screen feeding vendor) → pem → asn1 → connection → context (password/secret key names) → entropy → pii (off by default). Output markers are [REDACTED:<kind>], idempotent, and line-count preserving. Allowlisted shapes (Git SHAs, UUIDs) and data: base64 URLs survive.

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Fix: alignFor returns String? — change signature: `String? alignFor(int col) => col < aligns.length ? aligns[col] : null;` 3. `'` escaping of apostrophes in text — fine (valid HTML). 4. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Then html = renderMarkdown. So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. The first non-empty line is the image; h1 check fails on the image line; then cover-image check: start points at image line → matches → start++ → then the `# title` line remains in body.

Fix: handle sequence: loop — skip blanks; if line is cover image (and cover != null and not yet stripped) → strip; else if h1 == title → strip; else stop. Both, in either order.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Fix the builder: - In renderBlogPostPage: preprocess body: split lines; drop leading blank lines; if first line is `# <title-ish>` → drop; if first non-empty line is `![...](<cover>)` → drop and forceCover=true. Then html = renderMarkdown. Cover img emitted when `cover != null && (forcedCover || !body.includes...)` — after stripping, always emit post-cover when cover != null and we stripped it; if not stripped (cover not in body), emit post-cover too (post.html behavior). So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: false                  # per-server granularity (mcp:<server>)

# <project>/.fah/config.yaml — PROJECT scope: travels with the repo.
tools:

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

messages.preview: Two bugs to fix: duplicate `<h1>`/cover (post body has its own) and empty `text-align` in tables.

blocks.text:
Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

`: the body md already starts with `# ` (the post md has its own H1), and my template adds `<h1>$title</h1>`. Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Then html = renderMarkdown. So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. Also meta date: fine. Fix alignFor now. Also check: in `_renderTable`, `alignFor` used `aligns[col] != null ? aligns[col]! : ''` — replace with nullable.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): registered (exact values) → path (credential files) → credential (DOM form-field values) → vendor (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → prefix (indexOf pre-screen feeding vendor) → pem → asn1 → connection → context (password/secret key names) → entropy → pii (off by default). messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.
