Rather than retyping the entire FAQPage and HowTo content (huge, error-prone), I'll do this surgically with a small script: parse index.html, extract the three JSON blocks, wrap nodes into @graph. But hand-authoring the edit via hashline would need the whole content anyway. A Dart script is more reliable. But then the result must be committed — fine, it's a one-time transformation.

Actually simpler: do the edit with a python/dart one-liner that:
1. Reads site/index.html.
2. Extracts the three `<script type="application/ld+json">...</script>` blocks, parses JSON, takes each object's content minus @context.
3. Builds new structure: @context + @graph [Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication (modified author → @id, + sameAs), SoftwareSourceCode, FAQPage, HowTo].
4. Writes back.

JSON pretty-print formatting will change (indent 2, same style). That's acceptable — "intentionally extended". But byte-stability REG for the *content*: text strings unchanged.

I'll write a throwaway script in /tmp and run it. Indentation: JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ') produces 2-space indent matching existing style. Key order: Dart maps preserve insertion order; JSON parse preserves order too (json.decode returns LinkedHashMap with source order). 

Then SoftwareApplication modifications: set author → {'@id': .../#org}, add sameAs after downloadUrl? Order: I'll insert sameAs right after 'codeRepository'. And SoftwareSourceCode after SoftwareApplication. Organization + WebSite first.

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

blocks.text:
Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

`: the body md already starts with `# ` (the post md has its own H1), and my template adds `<h1>$title</h1>`. Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Fix: alignFor returns String? — change signature: `String? alignFor(int col) => col < aligns.length ? aligns[col] : null;` 3. `'` escaping of apostrophes in text — fine (valid HTML). 4. Two-space/indent quirk: `$meta$bodyHtml </article>` — bodyHtml lines start at col 0; fine. 5. Duplicate h1 also in docs pages? DocsPage body drops the first H1 — good. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Fix the builder: - In renderBlogPostPage: preprocess body: split lines; drop leading blank lines; if first line is `# <title-ish>` → drop; if first non-empty line is `![...](<cover>)` → drop and forceCover=true. Then html = renderMarkdown. Cover img emitted when `cover != null && (forcedCover || !body.includes...)` — after stripping, always emit post-cover when cover != null and we stripped it; if not stripped (cover not in body), emit post-cover too (post.html behavior). So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. Also meta date: fine. Fix alignFor now. Also check: in `_renderTable`, `alignFor` used `aligns[col] != null ? aligns[col]! : ''` — replace with nullable.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. messages.preview: The FAQ/HowTo blocks are large; I'll do the @graph merge with a one-shot transform script to avoid transcription errors:

blocks.text:
Rather than retyping the entire FAQPage and HowTo content (huge, error-prone), I'll do this surgically with a small script: parse index.html, extract the three JSON blocks, wrap nodes into @graph. But hand-authoring the edit via hashline would need the whole content anyway. A Dart script is more reliable. But then the result must be committed — fine, it's a one-time transformation.

Actually simpler: do the edit with a python/dart one-liner that:
1. Reads site/index.html.
2. Extracts the three `<script type="application/ld+json">...</script>` blocks, parses JSON, takes each object's content minus @context.
3. Builds new structure: @context + @graph [Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication (modified author → @id, + sameAs), SoftwareSourceCode, FAQPage, HowTo].
4. Writes back.

JSON pretty-print formatting will change (indent 2, same style). That's acceptable — "intentionally extended". But byte-stability REG for the *content*: text strings unchanged.

I'll write a throwaway script in /tmp and run it. Indentation: JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ') produces 2-space indent matching existing style. Key order: Dart maps preserve insertion order; JSON parse preserves order too (json.decode returns LinkedHashMap with source order).

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

blocks.text:
Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

`: the body md already starts with `# ` (the post md has its own H1), and my template adds `<h1>$title</h1>`. Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Fix: alignFor returns String? — change signature: `String? alignFor(int col) => col < aligns.length ? aligns[col] : null;` 3. `'` escaping of apostrophes in text — fine (valid HTML). 4. Two-space/indent quirk: `$meta$bodyHtml </article>` — bodyHtml lines start at col 0; fine. 5. Duplicate h1 also in docs pages? DocsPage body drops the first H1 — good. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Fix the builder: - In renderBlogPostPage: preprocess body: split lines; drop leading blank lines; if first line is `# <title-ish>` → drop; if first non-empty line is `![...](<cover>)` → drop and forceCover=true. Then html = renderMarkdown. Cover img emitted when `cover != null && (forcedCover || !body.includes...)` — after stripping, always emit post-cover when cover != null and we stripped it; if not stripped (cover not in body), emit post-cover too (post.html behavior). So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

`: the body md already starts with `# ` (the post md has its own H1), and my template adds `<h1>$title</h1>`. Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): registered (exact values) → path (credential files) → credential (DOM form-field values) → vendor (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → prefix (indexOf pre-screen feeding vendor) → pem → asn1 → connection → context (password/secret key names) → entropy → pii (off by default). messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Works, but inner nodes kept their `"@context": "https://schema.org"` keys — redundant inside a @graph (harmless but sloppy; schema.org validators tolerate it, but cleaner to strip). Also array formatting: JsonEncoder.withIndent puts each element on its own line — acceptable but verbose for sameAs arrays of 1-2 items. Fine.

Let me strip the nested @context keys from graph nodes (except top). Quick tweak: in the transform, remove '@context' from each node. Also compact arrays? Leave. Re-run: but the transform already consumed the 3-block format. Easier: small sed-like edit via dart one-liner to remove the two `"@context": "https://schema.org",` lines that are inside graph nodes (lines 71-ish and the FAQPage one). They appear at known indentation (4 spaces). Lines: `    {` followed by `      "@context": "https://schema.org",`. Use python or dart to remove lines matching `^      "@context": "https://schema.org",$` — the top-level one has 2-space indent `  "@context"`. Let me do it.

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Fix: alignFor returns String? — change signature: `String? alignFor(int col) => col < aligns.length ? aligns[col] : null;` 3. `'` escaping of apostrophes in text — fine (valid HTML). 4. Two-space/indent quirk: `$meta$bodyHtml </article>` — bodyHtml lines start at col 0; fine. 5. Duplicate h1 also in docs pages? DocsPage body drops the first H1 — good. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Fix the builder: - In renderBlogPostPage: preprocess body: split lines; drop leading blank lines; if first line is `# <title-ish>` → drop; if first non-empty line is `![...](<cover>)` → drop and forceCover=true. Then html = renderMarkdown. Cover img emitted when `cover != null && (forcedCover || !body.includes...)` — after stripping, always emit post-cover when cover != null and we stripped it; if not stripped (cover not in body), emit post-cover too (post.html behavior). So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. Also meta date: fine. Fix alignFor now. Also check: in `_renderTable`, `alignFor` used `aligns[col] != null ? aligns[col]! : ''` — replace with nullable.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: false                  # per-server granularity (mcp:<server>)

# <project>/.fah/config.yaml — PROJECT scope: travels with the repo.
tools:
====

  • The legacy exact-value SecretRedactor masks values it was told

about by name (provider API keys, request_secret grants). Attached lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).

  • The layered RedactionPipeline catches secret-shaped content it was

Layers

Output markers are [REDACTED:<kind>], idempotent, and line-count preserving. Allowlisted shapes (Git SHAs, UUIDs) and data: base64 URLs survive.

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

2026-09-20 · Uladimir Klyshevich · also on LinkedIn ↗

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost
Cached reads~24B$0.15 / 1M~$3,600
Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000
Total40B≈ $17–20k

blocks.text:
Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

`: the body md already starts with `# ` (the post md has its own H1), and my template adds `<h1>$title</h1>`. Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Fix: alignFor returns String? — change signature: `String? alignFor(int col) => col < aligns.length ? aligns[col] : null;` 3. `'` escaping of apostrophes in text — fine (valid HTML). 4. Two-space/indent quirk: `$meta$bodyHtml </article>` — bodyHtml lines start at col 0; fine. 5. Duplicate h1 also in docs pages? DocsPage body drops the first H1 — good. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Fix the builder: - In renderBlogPostPage: preprocess body: split lines; drop leading blank lines; if first line is `# <title-ish>` → drop; if first non-empty line is `![...](<cover>)` → drop and forceCover=true. Then html = renderMarkdown. Cover img emitted when `cover != null && (forcedCover || !body.includes...)` — after stripping, always emit post-cover when cover != null and we stripped it; if not stripped (cover not in body), emit post-cover too (post.html behavior). So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. OK compare plainText both sides. Cover image line match: `RegExp(r'^!\[[^\]]*\]\(' + RegExp.escape(cover) + r'\)\s*$')`. Then in template: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Simplify: emit post-cover iff cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')). Same as before but with strip. Then body markdown render — remove the old h1/cover naturally. Also meta date: fine. Fix alignFor now. Also check: in `_renderTable`, `alignFor` used `aligns[col] != null ? aligns[col]! : ''` — replace with nullable.

Updated 2026-10-10 · IstiN

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: false                  # per-server granularity (mcp:<server>)

# <project>/.fah/config.yaml — PROJECT scope: travels with the repo.
tools:

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.

messages.preview: Two test bugs: directory entities come with a trailing slash (empty last segment), and the JSON-LD count threshold was wrong (7 blocks, not >10):

blocks.text:
`/docs//` — Directory('site/docs').listSync() gives entity whose uri.pathSegments.last is ''? Because path 'site/docs/dap' — pathSegments of a Directory entity... `Directory('site/docs').listSync()` returns entities with paths like 'site/docs/dap' — uri.pathSegments.last = 'dap'. But trailing slash? The entity path may be 'site/docs/dap' — hmm the test output shows slug='' for one entity — that's likely the entity 'site/docs' itself? No. pathSegments: for path 'site/docs/dap', segments = ['site','docs','dap'], last='dap'. Getting '' suggests path ends with '/': 'site/docs/dap/' — then last segment is ''. We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The bill

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Token typeVolume~Rate~Cost

Fresh input~14B$0.60 / 1M~$8,400
Output~2B$2.50 / 1M~$5,000

For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Not stripped but body contains cover elsewhere → don't duplicate, body renders it. Absent → emit post-cover. Let me restructure: ```dart var body = p.body.trimLeft(); final lines = body.split('\n'); var idx = 0; while (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim().isEmpty) idx++; var coverFromBody = false; if (idx < lines.length && _heading matches && plainText(group2) == plainText(title)) idx++; if (idx < lines.length && lines[idx].trim() == '![${...}]($cover)') { coverFromBody = true; idx++; } body = lines.sublist(idx).join('\n').trimLeft(); ``` Compare heading text: `RegExp(r'^#\s+(.+)$')` firstMatch(lines[idx].trim()) → plainText(h.group(1)) == plainText(p.title)? plainText strips markers; title has `(~$20k)` — plainText leaves it. '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover" alt="$title">' : ''}` — after strip, if coverFromBody, body doesn't contain it anymore... unless duplicated. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?

Today is the day when everyone can build a mobile app directly on their mobile device. It's finally approved by Apple and available in the App Store. Let me tell you a story about it.

40,000,000,000 tokens. 3 months of work. Zero lines of code written by a human.

That is what building >_Fa — my open-source agent harness in Dart — has cost so far. Star the repo and continue reading :). Try it in web https://fa1.dev.

When people hear the number, they hear a fuckup. Forty billion tokens sounds like setting money on fire.

So let's count the money first. Everyone loves counting other people's money.

The workload ran on the cheapest models that can still do the job — Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash — routed per task. At straight API prices, the mix looks like this:

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.
