messages.preview: Two bugs to fix: duplicate `<h1>`/cover (post body has its own) and empty `text-align` in tables.

blocks.text:
Issues found: 1. Duplicate `

`: the body md already starts with `# ` (the post md has its own H1), and my template adds `<h1>$title</h1>`. Also the cover image: body includes `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)` → rendered as `<p><img ...></p>` — post.html renders `.post-cover` class and skips if body includes it. Fix: drop the leading H1 from the body if it equals the title (like docs), and handle cover: if body includes the cover image, the rendered img should get class post-cover... simplest: in renderBlogPostPage, remove the leading `# <title>` line from body; for the cover, leave the body's own `<p><img></p>` (acceptable) or convert first image to post-cover class. Better: strip leading image paragraph and emit `<img class="post-cover">` when body includes cover (mirror post.html logic: `if (meta.cover && !body.includes('](' + cover))` → add cover img; else body renders it inline). For class, I can post-process: if body contains cover image, replace the first `<p><img src="../posts/$cover"` with `<img class="post-cover" ...`. Simple approach: - bodyForRender = body with leading title-h1 line removed. - html = renderMarkdown(bodyForRender) - if cover != null: if body contained '](' + cover → html = html.replaceFirst('<p><img src="../posts/$cover"', '<img class="post-cover" src="../posts/$cover"') and remove trailing '</p>'... messy. Alternative: always strip the leading cover-image line from the md before render, then always emit `<img class="post-cover">`. If body has cover elsewhere (not first), it renders inline. The post's first line after frontmatter is exactly the cover image. Implement: - remove leading `# <title>` line (if matches title). - remove leading `![...](cover)` line (if equals cover) → set flag → emit post-cover img. That's clean and deterministic. 2. `style="text-align: "` with empty align — bug: `alignFor` returns '' when null and cell() checks `align != null`. In `_renderTable` I pass `alignFor(c)` which returns String ('' or value) but cell expects String? — '' is not null → emits `text-align: `. Fix: alignFor returns String? — change signature: `String? alignFor(int col) => col < aligns.length ? aligns[col] : null;` 3. `'` escaping of apostrophes in text — fine (valid HTML). 4. Two-space/indent quirk: `$meta$bodyHtml </article>` — bodyHtml lines start at col 0; fine. 5. Duplicate h1 also in docs pages? DocsPage body drops the first H1 — good. Also table `**Total**` cell renders `<strong>` inside td — good. Fix the builder: - In renderBlogPostPage: preprocess body: split lines; drop leading blank lines; if first line is `# <title-ish>` → drop; if first non-empty line is `![...](<cover>)` → drop and forceCover=true. Then html = renderMarkdown. Cover img emitted when `cover != null && (forcedCover || !body.includes...)` — after stripping, always emit post-cover when cover != null and we stripped it; if not stripped (cover not in body), emit post-cover too (post.html behavior). So: emit post-cover whenever cover != null and it was the leading image or absent from body; if present elsewhere in body, still emit post-cover? post.html: adds cover only if body does NOT include it. Post-strip: body no longer includes it as leading; but my strip only handles leading. Rule: stripped → emit post-cover. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

blocks.text:
The H1 strip didn't work — still a duplicate `<h1>` in body. Why? plainText comparison: title = "We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?" — h1 line: `# We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?`. plainText strips `[`*_~#>]` — the `~` in `(~$20k)` gets stripped! plainText removes `~` chars → "($20k)" vs title plainText also strips → both stripped equally. Wait both sides go through plainText... title has `(~$20k)` → plainText → `($20k)`; h1 same → equal. Hmm should match.

Wait — maybe the first line isn't the h1. Body after stripFrontmatter: the md begins with a blank line, then `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)`, then blank, then `# title`. So order: image FIRST, then h1! My code checks h1 first, then image. The first non-empty line is the image; h1 check fails on the image line; then cover-image check: start points at image line → matches → start++ → then the `# title` line remains in body.

Fix: handle sequence: loop — skip blanks; if line is cover image (and cover != null and not yet stripped) → strip; else if h1 == title → strip; else stop. Both, in either order.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: false                  # per-server granularity (mcp:<server>)

# <project>/.fah/config.yaml — PROJECT scope: travels with the repo.
tools:
====

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.

No. pathSegments: for path 'site/docs/dap', segments = ['site','docs','dap'], last='dap'. Getting '' suggests path ends with '/': 'site/docs/dap/' — then last segment is ''. On some platforms listSync returns trailing slashes for dirs? Apparently here yes.

So threshold 10 wrong; also post.html? post.html has no ld+json. widgets? no. So checked=7. Lower expectation to >=7... better: >=6 and include a per-file reason. I'll assert checked == number of pages that should carry schema? Keep `greaterThanOrEqualTo(7)`? More robust: expect(checked, greaterThanOrEqualTo(7)) with comment. The first non-empty line is the image; h1 check fails on the image line; then cover-image check: start points at image line → matches → start++ → then the `# title` line remains in body.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. The H1 strip didn't work — still a duplicate `<h1>` in body. Why? plainText comparison: title = "We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?" — h1 line: `# We burned 40 billion tokens (~$20k) building a harness. Am I crazy?`. plainText strips `[`*_~#>]` — the `~` in `(~$20k)` gets stripped! plainText removes `~` chars → "($20k)" vs title plainText also strips → both stripped equally. Wait both sides go through plainText... title has `(~$20k)` → plainText → `($20k)`; h1 same → equal. Hmm should match.

Wait — maybe the first line isn't the h1. Body after stripFrontmatter: the md begins with a blank line, then `![...](assets/40b-cover.png)`, then blank, then `# title`. So order: image FIRST, then h1! My code checks h1 first, then image. The first non-empty line is the image; h1 check fails on the image line; then cover-image check: start points at image line → matches → start++ → then the `# title` line remains in body.

Fix: handle sequence: loop — skip blanks; if line is cover image (and cover != null and not yet stripped) → strip; else if h1 == title → strip; else stop. Both, in either order.

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Updated 2026-10-10 · IstiN

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: false                  # per-server granularity (mcp:<server>)

# <project>/.fah/config.yaml — PROJECT scope: travels with the repo.
tools:

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Updated 2026-10-10 · IstiN

Tool availability (issue #19) decides, per tool id, whether the model sees a tool at all: a tools: config section stacks four scopes — global, project, session, runtime — over the host's hard capability floor, the deepest scope that mentions a tool wins, and a live gate applies the merged decision. Disabling a tool unregisters it (the prompt no longer offers it) and a late call answers a tombstone note instead of executing. Config can only turn a present tool OFF: a tool the platform cannot provide stays off no matter what any scope asks. Load modes (issue #680) are the orthogonal axis — how much of the ENABLED set is loaded into the schema at boot (see Load modes below).

A full example

# ~/.fah/config.yaml — GLOBAL scope: every project on this machine.
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:

blocks.text:
href="https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/backend-agent-mode.md"
  • The legacy exact-value SecretRedactor masks values it was told

about by name (provider API keys, request_secret grants). Attached lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).

  • The layered RedactionPipeline catches secret-shaped content it was

never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings, private-key contexts. Attach point: attachRedactionPipeline.

Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): registered (exact values) → path (credential files) → credential (DOM form-field values) → vendor (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → prefix (indexOf pre-screen feeding vendor) → pem → asn1 → connection → context (password/secret key names) → entropy → pii (off by default). Output markers are [REDACTED:<kind>], idempotent, and line-count preserving. Allowlisted shapes (Git SHAs, UUIDs) and data: base64 URLs survive.

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.

Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): registered (exact values) → path (credential files) → credential (DOM form-field values) → vendor (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → prefix (indexOf pre-screen feeding vendor) → pem → asn1 → connection → context (password/secret key names) → entropy → pii (off by default). messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

    ...

messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. messages.preview: Renderer bug: lazy multi-line list items split. Adding continuation-line support to the list parser:

blocks.text:
Renderer bug found: multi-line list items in redaction.md — items wrap across lines ("masks values it was told\nabout by name..."). My list parser stops the list at the first non-item line, so the continuation becomes a separate paragraph, splitting the item text. Need continuation-line support: after matching an item, absorb following lines that are not blank and don't start a new block construct (heading, fence, table, quote, hr) — i.e., plain lines — into the item text.

How to distinguish a list continuation from a new paragraph? Markdown rules: continuation lines are indented or the paragraph is "lazy". Simple heuristic: while next line is non-blank, not a list item (ul/ol), not heading/fence/hr/table-start/blockquote → append to current item text with a space. Risk: a paragraph immediately following a list without blank line — rare in these docs; and typical markdown style separates with blank lines. This lazy-continuation is exactly CommonMark's "lazy continuation". Implement: inside the item-collection loop, if line doesn't match ul/ol, check lazy continuation: non-empty, doesn't match any block start (heading/fence/hr/blockquote/table delimiter?) → append to last item's text, continue.

Table-start check requires lookahead of 2 lines — for continuation, treat a line containing '|' followed by delimiter as table → stop list. Use _isTableStart(lines, j).

Update _renderList collection loop in site_markdown.dart.

messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.

blocks.text:
`/docs//` — Directory('site/docs').listSync() gives entity whose uri.pathSegments.last is ''? Because path 'site/docs/dap' — pathSegments of a Directory entity... `Directory('site/docs').listSync()` returns entities with paths like 'site/docs/dap' — uri.pathSegments.last = 'dap'. But trailing slash? The entity path may be 'site/docs/dap' — hmm the test output shows slug='' for one entity — that's likely the entity 'site/docs' itself? No. pathSegments: for path 'site/docs/dap', segments = ['site','docs','dap'], last='dap'. Getting '' suggests path ends with '/': 'site/docs/dap/' — then last segment is ''. On some platforms listSync returns trailing slashes for dirs? Apparently here yes.

Fix: filter `slug.isNotEmpty` and use `entity.uri.pathSegments.where((s)=>s.isNotEmpty).last`. Same for blog dirs loop — the blog loop guards with md existence so '' was skipped there. Apply the same cleanup everywhere (also in the JSON-LD count test: expected >10 but got 7 — pages with ld+json: index(1 graph), blog/index(0), post(1), 5 docs(5) = 7. So threshold 10 wrong; also post.html? post.html has no ld+json. widgets? no. So checked=7. Lower expectation to >=7... better: >=6 and include a per-file reason. I'll assert checked == number of pages that should carry schema? Keep `greaterThanOrEqualTo(7)`? More robust: expect(checked, greaterThanOrEqualTo(7)) with comment. Let me count: index 1 block (1 graph node but 1 block), blog post 1, docs 5 → 7 blocks. assert >= 7.

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. messages.preview: Fixing the four issues (strip leading blanks, list trailing newline, plainText `#`, and a wrong test date vs the floor):

blocks.text:
Fixes: 1. `stripFrontmatter`: body after ` ---` is ` # Hello`? Original: `--- title: X --- # Hello`. My code: `text.substring(end + 4)` — end = index of ' ---' → substring from end+4 gives ' # Hello'?? Wait end points at the ' ' before '---'; end+4 skips ' ---'... '---' is 3 chars + the ' ' = 4 → lands after '---', i.e. at ' # Hello'; then replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^ '), '') removes ONE ' ' → ' # Hello'. Should strip all leading blank lines: use replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^\s+')... careful: would eat meaningful whitespace? Leading whitespace at doc start is never meaningful here. Use `RegExp(r'^ +')`. Test expects '# Hello'. OK. 2. `_emitList` writes without trailing newline — add `out.writeln()`? `_emitList` is called from renderMarkdown then continue loop; other blocks end with writeln. In renderMarkdown I call `_emitList(items, out, ...)` then `i = j; continue;` — _emitList writes '
    ...
' without newline. Add writeln after emit in renderMarkdown, or inside _emitList at the end of the top call. Simplest: in renderMarkdown: `_emitList(...); out.writeln();` But careful about freshness: adding ' ' after lists changes generated HTML → rebuild after fix. Fine, builder output is regenerated anyway. 3. plainText strips `#` — expected test output has '#19'. plainText is for meta descriptions; stripping '#' is questionable (issue #19 → issue 19). Remove `#` and `>` from the strip set: `s.replaceAll(RegExp(r'[`*_~]'), '')`. But then blockquote lines keep '>'? plainText is applied to titles/ledes, rarely quotes. Remove `#` only when at line start? Keep simple: strip `[`*_~]`. The h1-title comparison in renderBlogPostPage uses plainText on `# Title` after the `# ` was already consumed by the h1 regex — group(1) is title text. Comparing titles with `#`? "issue #19" in a title would compare unequally only if one side has # and other doesn't — both go through plainText equally. Removing '#' from strip set is safe. 4. Sitemap /blog/ lastmod: actual shows `https://fa1.dev/blog/` followed by `2026-09-20`? Wait the failure: expected `2026-01-02` right after blog loc. Actual must show 2026-09-20 — meaning blogLastmod wasn't lifted. Why? `newestPost = posts.first.lastmod` — posts list order from collectPages argument; in the test posts are [b(2026-01-02), a(2025-12-31)], newest = 2026-01-02 > 2026-09-20? NO — '2026-01-02' < '2026-09-20'! My test data dates are older than the floor. The real repo post is 2026-09-20. So the test expectation is wrong: floor wins for 2026-01-02. Fix test: use a post dated 2027-01-02 (newer than floor) to test the lift. Let me check the actual failure list — 6 failed: stripFrontmatter, ul 2+, ol/nested, lazy continuation, plainText, sitemap. Plus maybe 1 more? "20 passed, 6 failed". The 6th? Possibly 'blog post page' group something. Let me fix and rerun to see.

arguments.content:
### What changed fa1.dev becomes agent-legible end to end (gh-1476): a new deterministic build step (`scripts/build_site.dart` + minimal `scripts/site_markdown.dart`, pure Dart no deps) pre-renders every blog post and 5 curated docs pages to static no-JS HTML with per-page JSON-LD, regenerates `sitemap.xml` and `llms-full.txt`, and server-renders the blog index — all committed as artifacts and CI-gated against drift. ### Key decisions - **Deterministic lastmod**: front-matter `updated:`/`date:` for posts, an `updated` field in the docs registry, a registry table for static pages — no git/mtime, so CI checkouts rebuild byte-identically (this is what makes the staleness gate sound). - **One `@graph`** on the landing page: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareApplication (`sameAs` → GitHub + pub.dev) + SoftwareSourceCode (`codeRepository`, `runtimePlatform: Dart`) + the existing FAQPage/HowTo content preserved verbatim. - **robots.txt** names 11 AI crawlers with `Allow: /` and points at llms.txt / llms-full.txt; `User-agent: *` + sitemap line kept. - **llms-full.txt** (87 KB, under the 150 KB budget, builder-enforced) = llms.txt verbatim + every post and doc in full, each section headed by its canonical URL; llms.txt extended with Blog/Docs sections. - Blog body markdown stays single-source (site/blog/posts/*.md); HTML is generated, cover/H1 lifted into the template (`post.html` parity); legacy `post.html` still serves old links. - CI: `static` job runs `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check` (fails on any hand-edit/stale artifact); pages.yml rebuilds the layer at deploy and now triggers on `blog/**` + `docs/**` changes. ### How to verify ```bash dart scripts/build_site.dart --check # freshness gate (also in CI static job) dart test test/site/ test/scripts/ # 96 tests: no-JS crawl over loopback HTTP, # robots contract, sitemap integrity, # JSON-LD validation, builder units ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD MD[blog/posts/*.md + docs/*.md] --> B[scripts/build_site.dart] REG[date registries
front-matter / updated / static table] --> B B --> BP[/blog/slug/ index.html
BlogPosting JSON-LD/] B --> DP[/docs/slug/ index.html
TechArticle JSON-LD/] B --> SM[sitemap.xml
real lastmod] B --> LF[llms-full.txt
≤150 KB budget] B --> BI[blog index post list
generated markers block] CI[CI static gate
--check byte-diff] -.fails on drift.-> B PGH[pages.yml deploy] --> B ```

{"content":"### What changed fa1.dev becomes agent-legible end to end (gh-1476): a new deterministic build step (`scripts/build_site.dart` + minimal `scripts/site_markdown.dart`, pure Dart no deps) pre-renders every blog post and 5 curated docs pages to static no-JS HTML with per-page JSON-LD, regenerates `sitemap.xml` and `llms-full.txt`, and server-renders the blog index — all committed as artifacts and CI-gated against drift. ### Key decisions - **Deterministic lastmod**: front-matter `updated:`/`date:` for posts, an `updated` field in the docs registry, a registry table for static pages — no git/mtime, so CI checkouts rebuild byte-identically (this is what makes the staleness gate sound). - **One `@graph`** on the landing page: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareApplication (`sameAs` → GitHub + pub.dev) + SoftwareSourceCode (`codeRepository`, `runtimePlatform: Dart`) + the existing FAQPage/HowTo content preserved verbatim. - **robots.txt** names 11 AI crawlers with `Allow: /` and points at llms.txt / llms-full.txt; `User-agent: *` + sitemap line kept. - **llms-full.txt** (87 KB, under the 150 KB budget, builder-enforced) = llms.txt verbatim + every post and doc in full, each section headed by its canonical URL; llms.txt extended with Blog/Docs sections. - Blog body markdown stays single-source (site/blog/posts/*.md); HTML is generated, cover/H1 lifted into the template (`post.html` parity); legacy `post.html` still serves old links. - CI: `static` job runs `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check` (fails on any hand-edit/stale artifact); pages.yml rebuilds the layer at deploy and now triggers on `blog/**` + `docs/**` changes. ### How to verify ```bash dart scripts/build_site.dart --check # freshness gate (also in CI static job) dart test test/site/ test/scripts/ # 96 tests: no-JS crawl over loopback HTTP, # robots contract, sitemap integrity, # JSON-LD validation, builder units ```

≤150 KB budget] B --> BI[blog index post list

`/docs//` — Directory('site/docs').listSync() gives entity whose uri.pathSegments.last is ''? Because path 'site/docs/dap' — pathSegments of a Directory entity... `Directory('site/docs').listSync()` returns entities with paths like 'site/docs/dap' — uri.pathSegments.last = 'dap'. But trailing slash? The entity path may be 'site/docs/dap' — hmm the test output shows slug='' for one entity — that's likely the entity 'site/docs' itself? No. pathSegments: for path 'site/docs/dap', segments = ['site','docs','dap'], last='dap'. Getting '' suggests path ends with '/': 'site/docs/dap/' — then last segment is ''. On some platforms listSync returns trailing slashes for dirs? Apparently here yes.

Fix: filter `slug.isNotEmpty` and use `entity.uri.pathSegments.where((s)=>s.isNotEmpty).last`. Same for blog dirs loop — the blog loop guards with md existence so '' was skipped there. ## Summary of gh-1476 — fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization

**D1 — static pre-render build step**: `scripts/build_site.dart` (+ `scripts/site_markdown.dart`, a ~250-line dependency-free Markdown renderer) generates, deterministically from committed sources:
- `/blog/<slug>/` static pages with full raw-HTML content (the G1 fix — the blog was a JS shell) and `BlogPosting` JSON-LD
- `/docs/<slug>/` pages for 5 curated agent-quotable docs (tool-availability, redaction, migrating-from-claude-copilot-codex, hep, dap) with `TechArticle` JSON-LD
- a server-rendered post list in `/blog/` between generated-block markers (JS loader removed)
- `sitemap.xml` (12 URLs, real lastmod, 1.0 home / 0.8 posts) and `llms-full.txt` (87 KB, under the enforced 150 KB cap)

**D2** — robots.txt names 11 AI crawlers with `Allow: /` + llms pointers; **D3** — the three JSON-LD blocks merged into one validated `@graph` (Organization, WebSite, SoftwareSourceCode, `sameAs` on SoftwareApplication → GitHub + pub.dev; FAQ/HowTo content preserved byte-for-byte); **D5** — `site/llms.txt` extended with Blog/Docs/llms-full sections.

**Key design decision**: lastmod comes only from committed data (front-matter dates + registries, no git/mtime), so CI checkouts rebuild byte-identically — that's what makes the staleness gate sound. Verified both directions: `--check` passes on the committed tree and exits 1 on a hand-edit.

**Tests** (TDD, 96 passing in `test/site/` + `test/scripts/`): no-JS crawl over a real loopback HTTP server asserting distinctive source strings on every post/docs page, robots contract, sitemap-integrity, JSON-LD parse/validation per page, builder unit tests including 2+ item collections and a freshness-gate unit test. **CI**: `static` job runs `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check`; pages.yml rebuilds the layer at deploy and now triggers on `blog/**`/`docs/**`.

Not run: full repo-wide `dart test` (CI-sharded; all affected directories pass), post-deploy Rich Results Test (AC6, deploy-time).
